jobs.title: Founding Solutions Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Tolmo

Tolmo is cybersecurity for the age of AI. Coding agents now ship software faster than any human team can review or secure it; 100+ pull requests per engineer per week is no longer an outlier, and attackers are using the same agents to find and exploit weaknesses in days, not months. The old playbook of quarterly pentests and endless alert queues breaks at this speed.

We're building a new security playbook. Tolmo runs a fleet of AI security agents that reason over a live graph of your entire production system (code, CI, cloud, and telemetry) and continuously attack a faithful copy of it like a real adversary. Every finding arrives validated, with its blast radius and a remediation plan that lands in your workflow, ready for a coding agent to fix. Hours to integrate, days to your first validated finding.

We've done this before: Tolmo's founders built Sqreen (acquired by Datadog) and led security products that thousands of organizations trusted. We're backed by Accel and Y Combinator and just getting started.

The role

As our first Solutions Engineer, you're the technical heart of every customer conversation: you prove, hands-on, that Tolmo does what we say. You'll partner with founders and sales to turn skeptical security and engineering leaders into believers, and feed what you learn in the field directly back into the product.

This is an early, high-ownership seat. You won't inherit a polished playbook; you'll help write it. Expect a typical day to span summarizing security findings for a proof-of-value in a customer's cloud, walking a security engineer through blast-radius evidence, scripting a CISO-level demo against our production graph, and filing the feature gap that wins our next deals. You'll work across our market: digital-native enterprises with sprawling estates and AI-native companies shipping at agent speed.

What you'll do

  • Run technical discovery that surfaces a customer's real exposure: how fast they ship, where review breaks, and what a breach would cost them.

  • Design and deliver tailored demos that show how Tolmo reasons over their production graph and surfaces risk & remediation plans their current processes struggle with.

  • Own proofs-of-value end to end: qualify pains, define success criteria, and drive to first validated findings and a confident technical win.

  • Be the trusted technical advisor across the buying group, translating deep detail for security engineers, VP Engineering, and the CISO or CIO alike.

  • Author clear, persuasive responses to security questionnaires and RFPs, covering data handling, deployment model, and pentest evidence.

  • Coordinate with Tolmo security leads to schedule & deliver agent-assisted pentesting campaigns for proofs-of-value and customers.

  • Close the loop with product and engineering, carrying field signal back to shape what we build next.

  • Build the proof-of-value playbooks and reusable assets that make every AE and future SE faster.

What we're looking for

  • You own technical conversations end to end with customers: running discovery, delivering a tailored demo, and driving a proof-of-value to a technical win.

  • You translate deep technical detail into clear business value for engineers and executives alike.

  • You're hands-on: comfortable across cloud (AWS, GCP, or Azure), CI/CD, code, and the terminal, and you pick up unfamiliar stacks quickly.

  • You build with AI coding agents daily (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor) to prototype demos, integrations, and proof-of-value environments fast.

  • You think like an attacker: you understand how real systems break and chain together, not just how they're built.

  • You own ambiguity: energized by defining how something works, not just executing a process.

Nice to have

  • Hands-on offensive security: penetration testing, red teaming, or bug bounty work. Certifications like OSCP, OSEP, or CRTO are a strong signal; Security+, CISSP, or CEH are welcome too. None are required.

  • Experience selling to or working alongside security and engineering teams at enterprises or AI-native companies.

  • Familiarity with application and cloud security tooling (SAST, SCA, DAST, SIEM) and compliance frameworks (SOC 2, PCI, ISO 27001).

  • Prior startup, forward-deployed, or solutions-architecture experience.

  • Experience building a solutions engineering or solutions architecture org from the ground up.

Compensation & benefits

  • On-target earnings: 170,000–280,000, depending on level and experience (roughly 70% base / 30% variable).

  • Early-stage equity: you're joining early; you'll own a real piece of what we build.

  • Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, and the equipment you need to do your best work.

  • Based in San Francisco; we work in person where we can. We consider exceptional remote candidates who work primarily Pacific hours and travel for customers and team.

Tolmo is building a team with wide-ranging backgrounds, perspectives, and paths into security; we think it makes our product and judgment better. If you're excited about this role but don't match every point above, we'd still like to hear from you. We're an equal opportunity employer and welcome applicants of every background.

jobs.title: Member of the Technical Staff, Software Engineering
jobs.descriptionHtml:
ABOUT TOLMO

Tolmo is cybersecurity for the age of AI. Coding agents now ship software faster than any human team can review or secure it; 100+ pull requests per engineer per week is no longer an outlier, and attackers are using the same agents to find and exploit weaknesses in days, not months. The old playbook of quarterly pentests and endless alert queues breaks at this speed.

We're building a new security playbook. Tolmo runs a fleet of AI security agents that reason over a live graph of your entire production system (code, CI, cloud, and telemetry) and continuously attack a faithful copy of it like a real adversary. Every finding arrives validated, with its blast radius and a remediation plan that lands in your workflow, ready for a coding agent to fix. Hours to integrate, days to your first validated finding.

We've done this before: Tolmo's founders built Sqreen (acquired by Datadog) and led security products that thousands of organizations trusted. We're backed by Accel and Y Combinator and just getting started.

THE ROLE

As a Member of the Technical Staff, you build the system that makes our agents good at security: the graph they reason over, the infrastructure they run on, and the agents themselves. There are no fixed lanes. In one week you might ship a new cloud integration, rework how the graph links an endpoint to the code that serves it, and tune an offensive agent so it chains two low-severity findings into a real exploit.

You'll work directly with the founders and a small team of engineers who ship to production every day, and who use coding agents as heavily as the customers we protect. You'll own problems end to end: talk to the customer, design the fix, ship it, and watch it run in production.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Build and extend the live security graph: crawlers that discover cloud, SaaS, and code resources, and the pipeline that turns them into a consistent model of a customer's production system.

- Design, evaluate, and improve AI security agents that pentest, triage, chain, and remediate findings, and build the evals that tell us whether they actually got better.

- Own services end to end across Go, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, graph databases, and AWS, from design through deployment and on-call.

- Make the platform safe to point at production: strict tenant isolation, egress controls, and secrets handling that customers' security teams will scrutinize.

- Work with customers and our security leads to turn real findings, misses, and false positives into product improvements.

- Set the engineering bar as we grow: code quality, review culture, tooling, and how we build with AI agents.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

- Strong software engineering fundamentals and a track record of shipping and owning production systems end to end.

- Fluency in at least one of Go or TypeScript, and the willingness to work across the stack.

- Experience with distributed systems, data pipelines, or cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP, or Azure).

- You build with AI coding agents daily (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor) and have opinions about how to make them reliable.

- Curiosity about how real systems break: you want to understand the attack, not just the alert.

- You own ambiguity: energized by defining how something works, not just executing a process.

NICE TO HAVE

- Offensive security experience: penetration testing, red teaming, bug bounty, or CTFs.

- Experience building LLM agents, evals, or agent tooling in production.

- Experience with graph data models or graph databases (Neptune, Neo4j, Memgraph).

- Background in application or cloud security tooling (SAST, DAST, CSPM, SIEM).

- Prior early-stage startup or founding-engineer experience.

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

- Base salary: [PAY RANGE], depending on level and experience.

- Early-stage equity: you're joining early; you'll own a real piece of what we build.

- Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, and the equipment you need to do your best work.

- Based in San Francisco; we work in person.

Tolmo is building a team with wide-ranging backgrounds, perspectives, and paths into security; we think it makes our product and judgment better. If you're excited about this role but don't match every point above, we'd still like to hear from you. We're an equal opportunity employer and welcome applicants of every background.

jobs.title: Member of the Technical Staff, Security Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Tolmo

Tolmo is cybersecurity for the age of AI. Coding agents now ship software faster than any human team can review or secure it; 100+ pull requests per engineer per week is no longer an outlier, and attackers are using the same agents to find and exploit weaknesses in days, not months. The old playbook of quarterly pentests and endless alert queues breaks at this speed.

We're building a new security playbook. Tolmo runs a fleet of AI security agents that reason over a live graph of your entire production system (code, CI, cloud, and telemetry) and continuously attack a faithful copy of it like a real adversary. Every finding arrives validated, with its blast radius and a remediation plan that lands in your workflow, ready for a coding agent to fix. Hours to integrate, days to your first validated finding.

We've done this before: Tolmo's founders built Sqreen (acquired by Datadog) and led security products that thousands of organizations trusted. We're backed by Accel and Y Combinator and just getting started.

The role

As a Research Engineer on Offensive Security, you make our agents attack like the best human red teamers, and then better. You'll research how real systems get broken, turn that knowledge into techniques, tools, and evaluations our agents can use, and prove it against real customer environments.

This sits between research and engineering. In one week you might reproduce a new exploit class, teach an agent to chain an SSRF into cloud credential access, build the harness that checks whether it actually got there, and review the findings it files for a customer. You'll work directly with the founders, our engineers, and the security leads who run pentests with our agents, and your work ships to production.

What you'll do

  • Exploit research: study techniques across web applications, APIs, cloud (AWS, GCP, Azure), CI/CD, and identity, and turn them into capabilities our agents use in the field.

  • Attack-path discovery: work out how individually minor weaknesses chain into real impact, and encode that reasoning over our live graph of code, cloud, and telemetry.

  • Red-team tooling: build the scanners, probes, sandboxes, and exploitation helpers our agents call while they work.

  • Evals and benchmarks: design environments, including intentionally vulnerable targets, that measure whether our agents find, exploit, and validate real vulnerabilities, and keep false positives out.

  • Field validation: review agent findings from customer engagements, and turn every miss into a test case and an improvement.

  • Staying ahead: track new CVEs, exploitation research, and attacker tradecraft, and get them into the product within days.

What we're looking for

  • Deep hands-on offensive security experience: penetration testing, red teaming, exploit development, or vulnerability research.

  • A track record that shows it: CVEs, bug bounty results, CTF wins, published research, or talks.

  • Strong engineering skills: you write production-quality code (Go, TypeScript, or Python) and build tools other people rely on, not just one-off scripts.

  • Solid understanding of modern application and cloud architectures and how they fail: auth, access control, SSRF, injection, misconfigured IAM, exposed secrets, supply chain.

  • You build with AI coding agents daily (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor) and are curious about how far autonomous agents can take offensive work.

  • Sound judgment about safety and scope: you know how to test production-like systems without causing harm.

Nice to have

  • Certifications like OSCP, OSEP, OSWE, or CRTO. None are required.

  • Experience building or evaluating LLM agents, or applying machine learning to security problems.

  • Cloud security depth: privilege escalation in AWS, GCP, or Azure, Kubernetes, and container escapes.

  • Experience on an internal red team or at a security consultancy.

  • Contributions to open-source offensive tooling.

Compensation & benefits

  • Competitive salary, depending on level and experience.

  • Early-stage equity: you're joining early; you'll own a real piece of what we build.

  • Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, and the equipment you need to do your best work.

  • Based in San Francisco; we work in person.

Tolmo is building a team with wide-ranging backgrounds, perspectives, and paths into security; we think it makes our product and judgment better. If you're excited about this role but don't match every point above, we'd still like to hear from you. We're an equal opportunity employer and welcome applicants of every background.

About Tolmo

Tolmo is cybersecurity for the age of AI. Coding agents now ship software faster than any human team can review or secure it; 100+ pull requests per engineer per week is no longer an outlier, and attackers are using the same agents to find and exploit weaknesses in days, not months. We've done this before: Tolmo's founders built Sqreen (acquired by Datadog) and led security products that thousands of organizations trusted. We're backed by Accel and Y Combinator and just getting started.

The role

Security tools have a reputation: dense, noisy, and built for specialists who tolerate them. We think that's a design failure, not a law of nature. As a Software Engineer on Product, you build the surfaces where people meet our agents, and you make them feel fast, clear, and trustworthy.

You'll own Mission Control, where teams watch a fleet of agents work in real time, and the findings workflows that take a validated vulnerability from "what is this?" to "fixed" in as few steps as possible. The work is full-stack: you'll shape the API and data model as much as the pixels, because a great interface usually starts with the right data underneath it.

You'll work directly with the founders, our designer, and customers, and you'll have real say in what we build, not just how.

What you'll do

  • Mission Control: build the live view of agent activity, so people can see what an autonomous agent is doing, why, and how confident it is, without drowning in logs.

  • Findings workflows: design and ship how findings are triaged, explained, assigned, and fixed, including blast radius, evidence, and the handoff to a coding agent.

  • Full-stack ownership: take features from a rough idea through API design, data model, and UI to production, and follow them after launch.

  • Craft and polish: sweat the details that make software feel good: speed, empty states, keyboard flows, copy, and the small interactions nobody asks for but everyone notices.

  • Learn from customers: sit in on customer calls, watch people use the product, and turn friction into fixes within days.

  • Raise the bar: help shape our design system, front-end architecture, and how the team thinks about product quality.

What we're looking for

  • Taste. You can tell when something is off, explain why, and fix it. You have shipped products you're proud of, and you can show us.

  • Strong full-stack engineering skills, with deep experience in TypeScript and React and comfort working on APIs and databases.

  • A track record of owning product features end to end, from ambiguous problem to polished, shipped experience.

  • Care for UX at every level: information architecture, interaction design, performance, and accessibility.

  • Comfort with complex, data-heavy interfaces, and the judgment to make them simple without hiding what matters.

  • You build with AI coding agents daily (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor) and ship fast without letting quality slip.

Nice to have

  • Experience building developer tools, security, infrastructure, or observability products.

  • Experience designing interfaces for AI or agentic products, where trust and transparency matter.

  • Design skills of your own: you're comfortable in Figma, or you prototype straight in code.

  • Experience with real-time interfaces, graph visualization, or large data sets in the browser.

  • Prior early-stage startup or founding-engineer experience.

Compensation & benefits

  • Competitive salary, depending on level and experience.

  • Early-stage equity: you're joining early; you'll own a real piece of what we build.

  • Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, and the equipment you need to do your best work.

  • Based in San Francisco; we work in person.

Tolmo is building a team with wide-ranging backgrounds, perspectives, and paths into security; we think it makes our product and judgment better. If you're excited about this role but don't match every point above, we'd still like to hear from you. We're an equal opportunity employer and welcome applicants of every background.

You'll work directly with the founders, our designer, and customers, and you'll have real say in what we build, not just how.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Mission Control: build the live view of agent activity, so people can see what an autonomous agent is doing, why, and how confident it is, without drowning in logs.

 - Findings workflows: design and ship how findings are triaged, explained, assigned, and fixed, including blast radius, evidence, and the handoff to a coding agent.

 - Full-stack ownership: take features from a rough idea through API design, data model, and UI to production, and follow them after launch.

 - Craft and polish: sweat the details that make software feel good: speed, empty states, keyboard flows, copy, and the small interactions nobody asks for but everyone notices.

 - Learn from customers: sit in on customer calls, watch people use the product, and turn friction into fixes within days.

 - Raise the bar: help shape our design system, front-end architecture, and how the team thinks about product quality.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Taste. You can tell when something is off, explain why, and fix it. You have shipped products you're proud of, and you can show us.

 - Strong full-stack engineering skills, with deep experience in TypeScript and React and comfort working on APIs and databases.

 - A track record of owning product features end to end, from ambiguous problem to polished, shipped experience.

 - Care for UX at every level: information architecture, interaction design, performance, and accessibility.

 - Comfort with complex, data-heavy interfaces, and the judgment to make them simple without hiding what matters.

 - You build with AI coding agents daily (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor) and ship fast without letting quality slip.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience building developer tools, security, infrastructure, or observability products.

 - Experience designing interfaces for AI or agentic products, where trust and transparency matter.

 - Design skills of your own: you're comfortable in Figma, or you prototype straight in code.

 - Experience with real-time interfaces, graph visualization, or large data sets in the browser.

 - Prior early-stage startup or founding-engineer experience.


COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

 - Competitive salary, depending on level and experience.

 - Early-stage equity: you're joining early; you'll own a real piece of what we build.

 - Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, and the equipment you need to do your best work.

 - Based in San Francisco; we work in person.

Tolmo is building a team with wide-ranging backgrounds, perspectives, and paths into security; we think it makes our product and judgment better. If you're excited about this role but don't match every point above, we'd still like to hear from you. We're an equal opportunity employer and welcome applicants of every background.

jobs.title: Research Engineer, AI Security
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Tolmo

Tolmo is cybersecurity for the age of AI. Coding agents now ship software faster than any human team can review or secure it; 100+ pull requests per engineer per week is no longer an outlier, and attackers are using the same agents to find and exploit weaknesses in days, not months. The old playbook of quarterly pentests and endless alert queues breaks at this speed.

We're building a new security playbook. Tolmo runs a fleet of AI security agents that reason over a live graph of your entire production system (code, CI, cloud, and telemetry) and continuously attack a faithful copy of it like a real adversary. Every finding arrives validated, with its blast radius and a remediation plan that lands in your workflow, ready for a coding agent to fix. Hours to integrate, days to your first validated finding.

We've done this before: Tolmo's founders built Sqreen (acquired by Datadog) and led security products that thousands of organizations trusted. We're backed by Accel and Y Combinator and just getting started.

The role

Our product is only as good as our agents' judgment. As a Research Engineer on AI Security, you make that judgment better and measurably so: how our agents plan, reason over a graph of a customer's production system, decide what is worth testing, and know when a finding is real.

This sits between research and engineering. In one week you might design an eval that catches a new class of false positive, change how an agent plans a multi-step investigation, compare models on a hard benchmark, and harden the agents themselves against prompt injection from the systems they inspect. You'll work directly with the founders, our engineers, and the security leads who run pentests with our agents, and your work ships to production.

What you'll do

  • Agent reasoning: improve how our agents plan, use tools, and reason over a live graph of code, cloud, and telemetry, so they reach real findings faster and with fewer dead ends.

  • Evaluation: build the evals, benchmarks, and graders that tell us whether an agent actually got better, and make them part of how every change ships.

  • Model selection and tuning: compare models, prompts, and agent designs on cost, latency, and quality, and turn the results into production decisions.

  • Model and agent security: defend our agents against prompt injection, data exfiltration, and manipulation by the very systems they test, and research the security of LLM-based applications our customers build.

  • Reliability at scale: make long-running agents dependable across thousands of runs: verification, self-checks, and sensible stopping.

  • Learning from the field: study agent runs from customer engagements, find where reasoning broke, and turn each failure into an eval and a fix.

What we're looking for

  • Hands-on experience building, evaluating, or improving LLM-based agents or systems in production.

  • A rigorous, empirical approach: you design experiments, distrust single anecdotes, and let the evals decide.

  • Strong engineering skills: you write production-quality code (Python, TypeScript, or Go) and build tools other people rely on.

  • A working understanding of security, or a strong drive to learn it fast: how real systems are attacked and how findings are validated.

  • Familiarity with LLM security risks such as prompt injection, jailbreaks, and tool misuse.

  • You build with AI coding agents daily (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor) and have opinions about what makes them reliable.

Nice to have

  • Research background in machine learning, AI safety, or security: publications, open-source work, or talks.

  • Offensive security experience: penetration testing, red teaming, bug bounty, or CTFs.

  • Experience with reinforcement learning, fine-tuning, or synthetic data generation for agents.

  • Experience with graph data models or reasoning over structured data.

  • Prior early-stage startup experience.

Compensation & benefits

  • Competitive salary, depending on level and experience.

  • Early-stage equity: you're joining early; you'll own a real piece of what we build.

  • Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage, and the equipment you need to do your best work.

  • Based in San Francisco; we work in person.

Tolmo is building a team with wide-ranging backgrounds, perspectives, and paths into security; we think it makes our product and judgment better. If you're excited about this role but don't match every point above, we'd still like to hear from you. We're an equal opportunity employer and welcome applicants of every background.
